chapter: Joe Liggins and back to Kid Ory
title: Buster Wilson
summary: Joe remembers Buster Wilson from Mississippi as a gentleman and friend who played like Jelly Roll.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Anyway, getting back to Ory and them, and Tudie... Well, there's no point in me asking you a whole lot about Tudie, because as I said, he's covered, and so is Blakeney on the Rutgers things that I did. And we've talked about Mutt. But Buster. Buster Wilson.
Buster was one of the nicest gentlemen I eve met in the music business. He was every bit a gentleman.

Buster originally was from Mississippi, I believe. What I learned is that Buster developed... Him and Jelly Roll used to live together at one time, and they was very good friends -- and Buster played a lot like Jelly. Buster drank, drank a lot of liquor. That's probably what helped put him away, really. But a nice man, a nice guy... Buster and I was real good friends. I really liked Buster. Better than anybody in that Kid Ory band, for that matter, you know.
Well, he didn't seem, from what I could gather, like he was involved in that New Orleans cliquey sort of thing. You know what I mean? Because he wasn't from there, I guess.
Oh, no, he wasn't from New Orleans. Unh-uh. And then he said Jelly Roll had the influence on his piano style. And he did, if you would listen to him. He played a lot like Jelly Roll.
